1 A bug in the web layer is live. Users hit it right now.
2 You fix it and run one command. Capgo signs and publishes bundle 1.0.1.
3 The app checks Capgo and downloads the bundle in the background. Nothing interrupts the user.
4 The user leaves the app. The new bundle waits, ready for the next launch.
5 Next launch opens 1.0.1. The fix is live without a store review.
6 The app calls notifyAppReady(). If it never does, Capgo rolls back to the last working bundle.
1 A Capacitor app has two layers: the web layer (JS, CSS, HTML, assets) and the native shell (Swift,
2 A web-layer change ships as a live update. The CLI checks it is OTA-safe before upload.
3 A native change is stopped. The CLI tells you it needs a new binary through store review.
4 Store rules stay intact: native code always goes through review, web fixes never wait for it.
2 Capgo compares file checksums with what devices already have.
3 Only the 3 changed files travel: 180 KB instead of 4.2 MB.
4 The device rebuilds 1.0.1 from files it already has, verifies it, and waits for next launch.

3 Promote it to production at 25%. No new binary, no store review.
4 Errors spike on 2.6.0. Capgo shows which devices fail and why.
5 One click rolls production back to 2.5.0. Devices return to the known-good bundle.
6 Ship the fix as 2.6.1 and roll it out to 100%.
